source: FindMyPast — England Births & Baptisms 1538-1975 and England Marriages 1538-1973 (FamilySearch index); National Burial Index (Gloucestershire FHS); 1851 census
lede: For most of this archive's life the Saniger line was the thing it could not test. Six generations of it came from a family tree, and FreeREG's transcript of Berkeley St Mary the Virgin stops in 1677. Every one of those generations is now on a parish record, and the tree was right at every step.

verdict: Three baptism dates match the tree to the day, across a hundred and thirty years. One death date is ten months out. One marriage — Thomas Saniger to Catherine Cotton in 1769 — the tree did not have at all. On the evidence the compiler of this tree had seen the Berkeley register, or something copied faithfully from it, and this archive spent months treating their work as unevidenced assertion because it could not reach the same book.
cotton: Catherine Cotton herself goes no further. She marries at Berkeley in April 1769 and there is no baptism for her in the parish, so where she came from is open — the one new question this work has created rather than closed.
gap: And Hannah's own baptism remains missing, for a reason now established by control test: FindMyPast reaches Berkeley only through the FamilySearch index, and that index is partial. Her father's other children are in it and she is not. The original register at Gloucestershire Archives is what is left.
